## Bounded literature pass on Schinzel 1963, the Patras chapter and a later Schinzel-line thesis (baseline ea06c95)

### 1. Conclusion

**No direct match in the inspected sources, and two primary sources are still unread.**

- **Schinzel 1963 (Lehmer numbers I):** I could not get the full text. The publisher page links to a CC-BY PDF, but the download redirects to a mirror that returned HTTP 403 on both http and https. I did find a secondary restatement of its Theorem 1 in a 2007 Waterloo PhD thesis by Juricevic, and I read the relevant pages of that thesis myself. At our parameters (L,M)=(8,−1), that theorem only says U_n has **at least two primitive prime divisors** for odd n divisible by 3 with n ≥ 9. It says nothing about nonsquareness, odd valuation or quadratic characters, so it does not cover the Mersenne-weight criterion or the general norm exclusion. This is based on the restatement, not the original paper.
- **Rotkiewicz, Patras 1984 chapter (Reidel 1986):** not accessible. I found no SpringerLink chapter page, and my two guessed Springer DOIs both returned 404. It stays an unread full-text lead, not cleared.
- **Later sources:** the strongest descendant of Schinzel I/II/III is the Juricevic thesis. It counts primitive divisors and does not supply exact valuations or characters.

This is not a novelty claim. The general target-three claim and Erdős #132 remain unresolved.

### 2. Source table

| Source | Scope | Hypotheses → our notation | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Schinzel, *On primitive prime factors of Lehmer numbers I*, Acta Arith. 8 (1963) 213–223, DOI 10.4064/aa-8-2-213-223. [IMPAN page](https://www.impan.pl/en/publishing-house/journals-and-series/acta-arithmetica/all/8/2/95171/on-primitive-prime-factors-of-lehmer-numbers-i), [EuDML](https://eudml.org/doc/207291) | **Bibliographic, plus a theorem statement via a secondary source.** Full text blocked (redirect to `matwbn.icm.edu.pl/ksiazki/aa/aa8/aa8113.pdf` returned 403 ×2; EuDML returned ECONNRESET). | Juricevic says Juricevic Lemma 1.31 is Schinzel [24, Thm 1] made explicit. It assumes a real Lehmer pair (L>0, L−4M>0, gcd(L,M)=1), with κ the squarefree kernel of M·max(L−4M, L), η=1 if κ≡1 (mod 4) and η=2 otherwise, n>4, n≠6, and n/(ηκ) an odd integer. The conclusion is that u_n has at least two primitive divisors, except for finitely many listed cases. For (8,−1): κ=k(−12)=−3, η=1, so the condition holds exactly for odd n divisible by 3, n ≥ 9. (8,−1) is not in the exception table (Table 1.2 has (12,8,1), which is M=+1). Check: U_9=8721=3³·17·19, primitive divisors 17 and 19. | A count of primitive divisors only. No exact valuation, so nonsquareness of N_e does not follow. No character statement. **Does not subsume our result.** The original's other theorems are unchecked. |
| R. Juricevic, *Lehmer Numbers with at Least 2 Primitive Divisors*, PhD thesis, Waterloo 2007. [uwspace](https://uwspace.uwaterloo.ca/bitstreams/dc24ca7f-d2c2-400f-b42d-57719f0e532e/download) | **Partial full-text reading:** printed pp. 1–6, 12–21 and the bibliography pp. 100–102. Chapters 2–5 not read. | Lemma 1.26 (p.13): for M<0 and odd n, u_n(α,β) = u′_{2n}/u′_n for the associated pair (here (12,1)), and Φ_{2n}(α′,β′) = Φ_n(α,β). This independently confirms our e↔2e identification N_e = Φ_{2e}(λ,λ⁻¹). Lemma 1.24.5 (p.12; credited to Lehmer, proved by Stewart): if p>2 divides u_m, then p exactly divides u_{mp}/u_m. Lemma 1.25 (Stewart 1977, Lemma 6): the non-primitive prime divides Φ_n at most once; all other prime factors are ≡ ±1 (mod n). | Standard tools only. No square, character or Mersenne statement in the pages read. |
| A. Rotkiewicz, *Problems on Fibonacci numbers and their generalizations*, in Philippou–Bergum–Horadam (eds.), *Fibonacci Numbers and Their Applications* (Patras 1984), Math. Appl. 28, Reidel 1986, 241–255; MR87k:11025, Zbl 0594.10004. Listed on [Rotkiewicz's IMPAN page](https://www.impan.pl/~rotkiewi/) | **Bibliographic only** (plus the earlier reported zbMATH review). No SpringerLink chapter found; `link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-94-009-4311-7` and a guessed chapter URL returned 404. | Not applicable. | **Blocked, unread.** Not cleared. |
| Schinzel, Lehmer numbers II, Acta Arith. 8 (1963) 251–257, and III, Acta Arith. 15 (1968) | **Bibliographic only.** Juricevic p.17 describes II as giving ≥ r primitive divisors for r = 3, 4, 6. | Same Aurifeuillian-type primitive-count framework. | Lead only; same type of conclusion. |

**Small derivation from the standard lemma (not a literature subsumption).** Take e = 3^k with k ≥ 2. Then N_e = U_{3^k}/U_{3^(k−1)}. Since 3 divides U_3 = 9, Lemma 1.24.5 makes v₃(N_e) = 1, so N_e is not a square. For e = 3 the conclusion fails: N_3 = U_3 = 9 is a square. Neither case is covered by our criterion, because w(3) = 1 would force 2^(t−2) = 1, i.e. t = 2, which the criterion excludes. For k ≥ 2, nothing here is claimed about N_e/3.

### 3. Ready-to-use edits

**LITERATURE_REVIEW132.md, replace items 2–4 of "Remaining leads" with:**

> 2. Rotkiewicz (1986, Patras chapter): full text not obtained in the November 2026 bounded pass. No SpringerLink chapter page was located; Springer URLs tried returned 404. Only the bibliographic record and a previously reported zbMATH review were seen. It remains an unread lead and is not cleared.
> 3. Schinzel, *On primitive prime factors of Lehmer numbers I* (correct title), Acta Arith. 8 (1963) 213–223. The publisher CC-BY link redirects to an ICM mirror that refused automated access (HTTP 403). Its Theorem 1 was seen only as restated and made explicit in Juricevic (2007, Lemma 1.31, Theorem 1.1, Table 1.2). At (L,M)=(8,−1), κ=−3 and η=1, so the theorem gives at least two primitive divisors of U_n for odd n ≡ 0 (mod 3), n ≥ 9. (8,−1) is not an exception. This is a count of primitive divisors, not an odd valuation, nonsquare or character result, so it does not imply our criterion. The original paper's other statements remain unread.
> 4. Juricevic (2007), partial full text (pp. 1–6, 12–21, bibliography). Lemma 1.26 confirms the odd-n identity u_n(8,−1) = u′_{2n}/u′_n with the associated pair (12,1). No square, character or Mersenne statement appears in the pages read.

### 4. Stopping recommendation

This bounded pass is enough. I recommend going back to the mathematical work on the general target-three norm problem.

The only literature that remains unread is the original Schinzel I/II/III texts and the Patras chapter. Everything seen so far from the Schinzel line is about counting primitive divisors, which cannot settle whether N_e is a square without valuation input. Record these as documented unread leads, not as prerequisites. If the user ever happens to supply PDFs, they could be checked, but that is optional and not a task for them.

The useful mathematical takeaway: Schinzel's Aurifeuillian splitting at (8,−1) when 3 divides e is a possible structural tool for the norm problem, but it is not a proof route as it stands.
